proposed_object: A learned tactic policy that turns a symbolic non-equivalence obligation into a legal separating experiment.
useful_distinction: This could amortize the computation of finding an experiment. Such a computational gain is distinct from reducing the number of executed experiments.
analytic_finding: Every query chosen by both strategies is a shortest one-primitive pairwise separator. With eight uniform candidates, first-separator search needs 4.375 queries on average (worst 7), versus 3 for balanced candidate splitting. With 32 candidates, the costs are 16.46875 versus 5. Separator construction alone does not determine identification efficiency.
scope_limit: This is an exact finite counterexample to an objective-level implication, not a native task, training run, theorem-prover timing experiment, or empirical refutation of an implemented learned tactic policy. Actual proof depth can differ from separator program length.
missing_operation: The answer lists generic tactics but does not define their typed transition rules, the symbolic-law-to-native compiler, or a learned update distinct from existing tactic-guided search. Source law annotations and proof search would have to be explicitly available and counted.
ablation_limit: Randomizing proof-state/tactic edges corrupts supervision for any learner of those pairs; degradation alone would not uniquely establish cross-law proof-construction transfer. A matched semantic-renaming control and target-only guided search would be necessary if this candidate were implemented.
prior_scope: TacticToe learns tactic selection from earlier proofs and uses it in MCTS. This constrains novelty of the learned-proof-policy component, but does not establish that the proposed cross-domain experimental combination is identical to TacticToe.
decision: Do not start native or GPU scaling for this written suggestion. No blanket rejection of proof-directed experimental design; a distinct implemented operation and matched computational/task gains would be needed.
